segmentation.prompt:
Given the following text, tell me where you would apply broad semantic breaks.
The purpose is coarse chunking for later categorization. Prefer a few large sections over many detailed sections.

Use natural boundaries such as headings, labeled sections, or clear changes in subject.
Keep related content together. Keep code, examples, instructions, and technical details with the section they belong to.
Do not split repetitive or line-oriented content into small pieces.

Return ONLY a valid JSON array of regexes with positive lookahead which I can use to run string split on in javascript.

Example response format: ["(?=regex-of-section-1)", "(?=regex-of-section2)"]

dimensions.name: task_intent
dimensions.prompt: Given this conversation, list the task intents that explain why work is being performed. Use concise programming terminology with lowercase snake_case names. Possible examples include bug_fixing, validation, performance_optimization, documentation, configuration, feature_implementation, investigation, or refactoring. These examples are not exhaustive; use other established programming terms when they describe the conversation more accurately. Include only intents supported by the conversation. Do not include technologies, tools, files, or technical areas.

dimensions.name: technical_area
dimensions.prompt: Given this conversation, list the technical areas where work is being performed. Use concise programming terminology with lowercase snake_case names. Possible examples include language_and_type_systems, cli, file_system, security, testing, build_tooling, networking, user_interface, api, concurrency, or dependency_management. These examples are not exhaustive; use other established programming terms when they describe the conversation more accurately. Include only areas supported by the conversation. Do not include task intents such as bug_fixing, validation, implementation, or investigation.

components.name: instruction
components.description: User requests, requirements, constraints, clarifications, corrections, or other directions defining what the agent should do.

components.name: agent_reasoning
components.description: Agent analysis, planning, interpretation, decision-making, or explanation used to determine next actions.

components.name: tool_call
components.description: Agent requests to execute tools, including file reads, searches, shell commands, code edits, or external operations.

components.name: tool_result
components.description: Outputs returned by tools, including file contents, search matches, command output, errors, and edit confirmations.

components.name: conclusion
components.description: Agent final answers, completed-work summaries, findings, recommendations, or explicit handoffs to the user.

dimensions.name: tool_call
dimensions.prompt: Given this conversation, list the specific tools or commands invoked by tool calls. Identify the concrete operation instead of abstracting it into a broad category. Use concise lowercase snake_case names matching the invoked tool or command, such as grep, rg, find, ls, file, cat, sed, git, npm, bun, tsc, read_file, write_file, edit_file, or generate_image. These examples are not exhaustive; use the actual tool or command found in the conversation. For shell tool calls, inspect the command and classify by its primary executable rather than using generic names such as shell, command_execution, search_tool, file_operation, or version_control. Include not_tool_call for content that is not a tool call.

components.name: file_content
components.description: Content returned from reading or inspecting one or more files.

components.name: search_result
components.description: Matches, paths, symbols, records, or other results returned by a search or lookup operation.

components.name: change_result
components.description: Confirmation, diff, status, or error returned after creating, editing, deleting, or otherwise modifying content.

components.name: test_output
components.description: Results from tests, type checks, linters, builds, validation commands, or other correctness checks.

components.name: command_output
components.description: Standard output, standard error, exit status, or execution details from a command not better classified as test_output.

components.name: submission_result
components.description: Result of submitting, publishing, uploading, committing, pushing, or sending completed work to an external destination.

components.name: not_tool_result
components.description: Content that is not a tool result, including instructions, agent reasoning, tool calls, and conclusions.

components.name: reason
components.description: Agent interprets evidence, explains behavior, evaluates possibilities, identifies causes, or derives a technical conclusion.

components.name: plan_next_step
components.description: Agent decides or states what action to take next, including files to inspect, commands to run, changes to make, or checks to perform.

components.name: recover
components.description: Agent responds to a failed command, invalid assumption, blocked approach, or unexpected result by choosing an alternative action.

components.name: re_evaluate
components.description: Agent revisits an earlier interpretation, plan, or conclusion after receiving new or contradictory evidence.

components.name: conclude
components.description: Agent determines that work is complete or summarizes a resolved finding within its reasoning. Use for internal conclusions, not final user-facing answers.

components.name: not_agent_reasoning
components.description: Content that is not agent reasoning, including user instructions, tool calls, tool results, and final user-facing responses.

components.name: error_reported
components.description: An error, failure, incorrect behavior, failing check, or unexpected result is first presented or observed without substantive diagnosis.

components.name: error_diagnosis
components.description: Content investigates, explains, or identifies the cause of a reported error using evidence, code inspection, logs, or reasoning.

components.name: error_correction
components.description: A change or action is proposed or performed to correct a diagnosed error, before successful resolution is confirmed.

components.name: error_fixed
components.description: Evidence confirms that the error is resolved, such as a passing test, successful command, correct output, or explicit verified conclusion.

components.name: error_re_correct
components.description: A previous correction failed, was incomplete, or introduced another problem, and a subsequent corrective action is attempted.

components.name: not_error
components.description: Content unrelated to an error lifecycle, including ordinary implementation, exploration, successful operations without prior failure, and general discussion.

dimensions.name: error_tool
dimensions.prompt: Given this conversation, list tools or tool categories associated with errors. Use concise lowercase snake_case programming terminology, such as compiler, type_checker, test_runner, shell, package_manager, version_control, file_editor, api_client, or build_system. These examples are not exhaustive; use other established terms when supported by the conversation. Include not_error for content that does not describe or expose an error. Avoid classifying by error cause, technical area, environment, or evaluation outcome.

dimensions.name: error_code
dimensions.prompt: Given this conversation, list code-related error categories. Use concise lowercase snake_case programming terminology, such as syntax_error, type_error, import_error, invalid_argument, null_reference, state_management_error, control_flow_error, interface_mismatch, or test_failure. These examples are not exhaustive; use other established terms when supported by the conversation. Include not_error for content unrelated to an error. Classify the defect expressed by code rather than the tool reporting it, execution environment, or evaluation outcome.

dimensions.name: error_environment
dimensions.prompt: Given this conversation, list environment-related error categories. Use concise lowercase snake_case programming terminology, such as missing_dependency, version_mismatch, permission_error, path_error, missing_file, invalid_configuration, unavailable_service, resource_exhaustion, or platform_incompatibility. These examples are not exhaustive; use other established terms when supported by the conversation. Include not_error for content unrelated to an error. Classify failures caused by runtime, system, dependency, configuration, or infrastructure conditions rather than source-code defects or evaluation outcomes.

dimensions.name: error_evaluation
dimensions.prompt: Given this conversation, list evaluation-related error categories. Use concise lowercase snake_case programming terminology, such as assertion_failure, regression, build_failure, lint_failure, type_check_failure, benchmark_regression, incomplete_validation, incorrect_output, or acceptance_failure. These examples are not exhaustive; use other established terms when supported by the conversation. Include not_error for content unrelated to an error. Classify failures revealed while checking correctness, quality, performance, or acceptance rather than the reporting tool, source-code defect, or execution environment.
